issues.description: Method SealSaloon.acceptSupplyDelivery(String,int,int): The problem statement's UML declares this method as public (notation: +acceptSupplyDelivery(String, int, int): void), but the provided solution implementation declares it with package-private visibility (signature: static void acceptSupplyDelivery(String name, int price, int quantity) — no explicit public). This discrepancy can confuse students about the intended API: whether acceptSupplyDelivery should be callable from other packages/classes (public) or intentionally restricted to package scope. It may also affect how students write test code or call the method from other classes.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the visibility explicit and consistent. Two acceptable resolutions: (A) Update the solution to match the UML/API in the problem statement by declaring the method public: 'public static void acceptSupplyDelivery(String name, int price, int quantity) { ... }'. Or (B) If package-private visibility is intended, update the problem statement/UML to remove the '+' and document that the method is package-private. Recommendation: prefer (A) to keep the method public as shown in the UML so it is clearly callable from other classes and matches the stated API.
